label: text
text: May Have to Give Up Hankow.

label: text

label: text
text: Sun Chuan-fang Advances on. Wuchang.

label: text
text:
From Out Special Correspondent.
Continuing their retreat on the most northerly sector of the Klingai-Hunan front, the Nationalists give the impression of falling back in preparation for a determined stand, rather than through inferiority in the field.

label: text
text: Marshall Sun Chuan-fang is now estimated to have 80,000 in Hupeh province, on the march to Wuchang. The southerners opposed to him there do not number more than 50,000, some of whom have been fighting for two months.

label: text
text: On the centre and south of this front—where the southern troops are comparatively fresh—there has been little of account during the last two days except that the Cantonese are retiring to preserve their alignment with those further north.

label: text
text: In the absence to date of a big, deciding battle, it is difficult to predict whether Sun Chuan-fang will capture Wuchang, Hanyang and Hankow.

label: text
text:
The southerners are now sopperilously near their line of communication with Canton that unless they stem the tide within a few days, they will be pushed out into the south-west of China, having then to make a detour home.
On Wednesday and Tuesday, the "5 province allies" were moving forward gradually, keeping in touch with the southerners, but trying to press back the whole of the northern sector.

label: text
text: Advanced, brigades of the southerners still hold strategic points, abutting into the allies' lines.

label: text
text: Chang Kai-shek's Position.

label: text
text: Sun Chuan-fang's main advance has been along the southern bank of the Yangtse, going up river close to the right bank, with the Wu-Han cities as his objective.

label: text
text: There is now an appreciable danger that the Cantonese will struck a dendly blow here.

label: text
text: Rather than face such a risk, it is surmised that General Chang Kai-shek will shorten his line by sacrificing Hankow, and concentrating on a stand between Yochow and Changsha.

label: text
text: The Cantonese are facing Sun Chuan-fang from the east and Yang Sen is marching down on them from the west.

label: text
text: Meanwhile General Yang, Sen's id portends an attack on the Nationalist rear, in Hupeh.

label: text
text: Race for the Spoils?

label: text
text: Further north, Marshal Wu Pei-fu still talks about a counterattack. Outposts of the Nationalist 8th army, stretched northwards from Hankow, are gradually coming back southwards, but Wu Pei-fu has yet to advance again. Should there be a southern debacle there may follow a unique race for control of Wu-Han between five contenders, viz. (1) Gen. Liu Tso-lung (who betrayed Wu Pei-fu and now occupies Hanyang as commander of 15th Nationalist Army); (2) Gen. Liu Yu-chen (defender of Wuchang and pro-Wu); (3) Sun Chuan-fang (going up the Yangtse); (4) Yang Sen (coming down the Yangtse); (5) Wu Pei-fu (from Honan province, in the north).

label: text
text: Attacks on the southern forces are reported from up and down River and from Han (Honan province?), extensive operations being in progress.

label: text
text: Seven nations were represented at the Miners' International Committee convoked to consider international measures to support the British miners. It adjourned till to-morrow without officially issuing any statement.

text: Messrs. A. J. Cook and Herbert Smith represented Great Britain. label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: NOT USING WHARF YET.

label: text
text: "Not until the boycott is officially finished," was the reply of Mr. John Arnold to-day when asked as to when the Steamboat Co.'s vessels were going alongside the wharves at Canton again.

label: text
text: The “China Mail” asked, in view of Chinese expectations that the Hong Kong, Canton and Macao Steamboat Co., Ltd., will take the lead in “restoring” communications,” would the steamboats go to the wharf instead of anchoring in the stream at Canton.

label: text
text: Mr. Arnold, as secretary, said that the company did not intend to do so until the boycott is actually and officially over.

label: text
text: Nor is there any truth in rumours that the Company has been overhauling the wharves at Canton. "None of the company's officials have been near the wharves for over a year," stated Mr. Arnold.

label: paragraph_title
text: / Wait & Little Longer.

label: text
text: There is therefore, little new to report in the way of a return to normal conditions as regards shipping.

label: text
text: The “outside” companies are waiting for a more definite development before putting their ships back on the river runs. Some are ready to go into dock for preliminary overhaul, a few are in running order, while one or two steamers may have to wait a little longer.

label: text
text: But it is likely that the Steamboat Co's "Lungshan" and the China Navigation Co's "Fanshan" (run in conjunction) will be the only boats for a few days more at least, and that they will continue to anchor in the river.

label: text
text: Reliable sources in Canton now state that more time has been needed to withdraw the pickets. October 5 is the first date promised, possibly October 10 and even a little later if necessary.

label: text
text: Beyond yesterday's reports there is nothing further to indicate the calling off of more pickets.

label: text
text: To the present state of affairs, Hong Kong can only point out that Mr. Eugene Chen categorically mentioned “on or before October 10 (most probably at the end of September),” while his second communique gave no date, the words reading “that arrangements have been made with the Strike Committee for the termination of the boycott.”

label: text
text:
Of course, Mr. Chen qualifies the second statement with:—
“To what extent this step will lead to a restoration of Chinese-British trade relations must depend on British policy……”

label: text
text: Actually the boycott has not ended yet as "Strike" activities are still in evidence at Canton itself, not mentioning any outport.

label: text
text: Chinese passengers for Hong Kong can now go unmolested into Shameen, whence they tranship by sampan or motorboat to the Hong Kong steamer. They are not interfered with. On the other hand, passengers going up from Hong Kong leave the boat in the stream and land wherever they can.

It is felt that an official announcement by the Canton Government may not be made. If the pickets are to be entirely demobilised by October 10, there will be no normality, it is thought. If the organizations continue to function an announcement will be hard to place.
